blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Run A starts project R in 2029 and run B starts it in 2031. One tool diffs the two runs' start variables; another diffs them project by project. What does each report for R?

options.text: Variables: one shift of two years. Projects: one drop and one add
options.says: This reverses them: x[R,2029] goes to 0 and x[R,2031] to 1, two variable changes, which a project diff reads as one shift.

options.text: Variables: one drop and one add. Projects: one shift of two years later
options.says: Right: two start variables change, but R is in both plans with different years, so a project diff reports one shift.

options.text: Variables: no change at all. Projects: one shift of two years later
options.says: Two start variables do change value; only the project's funding stays the same.

options.text: Variables: one shift of two years. Projects: no change, as R is in both
options.says: A project in both plans with different years is exactly what the shifted list holds.

origin.section: A Diff Compares Plans Project by Project, in Three Lists

questions.stem: Scenario S1 cuts a budget. S2 is S1 with project Q also forced in, and the S1 to S2 step costs $90k. Forcing Q in on the uncut base costs $140k. What does forcing Q in cost?

options.text: $140k, since an override is priced on the uncut base
options.says: There is no single base for an override; its cost depends on what changed before it.

options.text: $230k, since the $90k and $140k steps add up
options.says: Step costs add only along one path; these two start from different scenarios.

options.text: $50k, the gap between the $140k and $90k figures
options.says: The $50k gap is the interaction of the two changes, not a cost of either one.

options.text: $90k after the cut and $140k without it
options.says: Right: the cost of one change is given the others, as P024 cost $273k before the 2029 cut and $205k after it.

origin.section: Change One Input at a Time, or the Diff Cannot Be Charged to a Cause

questions.stem: Two runs with identical inputs, each stopping within a 0.5% relative gap, return plans in which two projects trade start years. Their NPVs differ by 0.02%. What does the diff show?

options.text: A near tie between two plans, not a decision about a project
options.says: Right: both plans are within the 0.5% gap, so either may be returned; the 0.02% difference is a coin toss on details.

options.text: A solver bug, since two finished runs should return one plan
options.says: No bug is needed: identical runs that stop within a gap may stop at either of two nearly equal plans.

options.text: A fault in the model, since the two plans should have matched
options.says: GridCap small's correct model has a second plan only $8k below its best.

options.text: A real decision, since the start-year moves need explaining
options.says: A diff is weighed by its NPV change; 0.02% inside a 0.5% gap is not a decision.

origin.section: A Diff Worth a Few Thousand Is a Near Tie, Not a Decision
